task_goal: Assess whether systematic differences in user satisfaction exist across four tourism domains (accommodation, indoor attractions, outdoor attractions, destination): harmonize to a common 1-5 scale, robust-Z-standardize per domain, report mean/std/95%CI per source, and run a one-way ANOVA (F, p, eta^2).

hypotheses.H0: The four domains share a common mean satisfaction level (mu_accommodation = mu_indoor = mu_outdoor = mu_destination) on the harmonized 1-5 metric / on robust-Z scores.
hypotheses.H1: At least one domain mean differs from the others.
hypotheses.decision_rule: two-sided alpha = 0.05 on the ANOVA F test; effect size interpreted alongside p (large n makes p near-certain).

accommodation.granularity: one row per short-term rental listing (listing-level rating)
accommodation.note: Nearly uniform across 1-5 (mean 3.28); the only source with a materially negative mode share. Uses only this one column; read with usecols to avoid loading 35MB of irrelevant price/host fields.

indoor_attraction.granularity: museum-month record (27 distinct museums, monthly rating repeated per venue)
indoor_attraction.note: Venue-level aggregate repeated over many months -> strong left skew and pseudo-replication; the effective independent n is ~27 venues, not 2676 rows.

outdoor_attraction.note: Truncated at a 3.0 floor: no 1-2 observations exist, so the raw 1-5 scale is de-facto censored and dispersion is not comparable in raw units. Mean 4.67, sd ~0.26.

destination.granularity: one row per transaction (individual tourist rating of an attraction)
destination.note: Rating is stored as text (or read as object) and MUST be coerced with pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') before any arithmetic; otherwise groupby mean silently drops/fails.

analysis_steps.name: load_and_extract
actions: Airbnb: read only usecols=['review rate number'] -> rename to value, source='accommodation'.
indoors: read usecols=['rating','mus_ID'] -> value=rating, source='indoor_attraction'; keep mus_ID for the venue-level sensitivity check.
outdoors: read usecols=['rate','park_id'] -> value=rate, source='outdoor_attraction'; keep park_id for sensitivity.

destination: read tx_clean.csv usecols=['Rating'] -> pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce'); if tx_clean.csv were absent, rebuild it by parsing the Transaction.xlsx OOXML stream (openpyxl unavailable in env; sharedStrings + sheet1.xml, dimension A1:G52931).
analysis_steps.check: row counts and valid_n must match data_profile.json (102273 / 2676 / 2923 / 52930) within 0 tolerance; mismatch => stop and re-inspect dtype coercion.

analysis_steps.name: harmonize_to_1_5
actions: clip to [1,5] (winsorize any out-of-range onto the boundary)

no min-max or ratio rescaling needed: all four variables already use a 1-5 metric (verified: accommodation 1-5, indoor 1-5, outdoor 3-5, destination 1-5; zero out-of-range values in the current data).
analysis_steps.rationale: Equal-interval 1-5 comparison is only defensible because no source uses a 10-point / 100-point / percentage scale. If a future refresh introduces such a source, map it linearly to 1-5 first and log the transform.

analysis_steps.name: robust_z_standardization
analysis_steps.formula: z = (x - median) / (1.4826 * MAD), MAD = median(|x - median|)
analysis_steps.fallback: MAD == 0 -> (x - median)/(IQR/1.349) -> (x - median)/sd (record scale_method per group)
analysis_steps.actions: compute median, MAD, robust_scale per source INDEPENDENTLY (each domain is centred on its own median and rescaled by its own robust spread), then transform all observations of that source.
analysis_steps.interpretation: z=0 is the domain's own typical (median) value and 1 unit = 1 robust SD of that domain, so between-domain z means measure how far each domain's central tendency sits from its own anchor, NOT raw satisfaction differences.

analysis_steps.name: source_statistics
analysis_steps.ci_method: normal-approximation / t with df=n-1 and t_crit from scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, n-1); with n>=2676 the two coincide to 4 decimals
analysis_steps.report_on: robust-Z scores (primary, as specified), and optionally the raw 1-5 means as a supplementary sanity table

analysis_steps.name: one_way_anova
actions: pool the four robust-Z vectors into one frame (source, z)
scipy.stats.f_oneway(z_accommodation, z_indoor, z_outdoor, z_destination) -> F, p
eta_squared = SS_between / SS_total, with SS_between = sum(n_g*(mean_g - grand_mean)^2), SS_within = sum over groups of sum((z - mean_g)^2)
also compute omega_squared = (SS_between - (k-1)*MS_within) / (SS_total + MS_within) as an unbiased companion
analysis_steps.p_value_handling: F is astronomically large; p underflows to 0.0 in float64. Write p as 0.0 but ALSO record p_display as '<1e-300' (or log10 p) in anova_detail.json so the result is not misread as an exact zero.
analysis_steps.effect_size_note: eta^2 ~ 0.019 is a SMALL effect (Cohen: 0.01 small, 0.06 medium, 0.14 large) even though p is decisive: the significance is driven by n~1.6e5, so the practical conclusion is 'differences are statistically certain but small in magnitude'.

analysis_steps.name: post_hoc_and_diagnostics
actions: pairwise Welch t-tests on all 6 pairs (does not assume equal variance, which is clearly violated here: z sd ranges 0.65 -> 2.10) with Cohen's d per pair
Levene / Brown-Forsythe test on the raw 1-5 values to document variance heterogeneity
skew + kurtosis per source to justify the robust Z (indoor skew ~ -2.5, outdoor truncated at 3.0)

sensitivity: re-run the ANOVA on VENUE-LEVEL means for FISETIO (aggregate months to one mean per mus_ID / park_id, n=27 and n=83) to remove monthly pseudo-replication; report whether the direction of the ordering and eta^2 sign survive. This is the single most important robustness check because ~1900 of the indoor rows are repeated venue aggregates.

analysis_steps.name: write_outputs_and_validate
actions: write output1.csv, output2.csv, anova_detail.json, posthoc.json, and a findings summary
validate schemas, dtypes, no NaN, CI ordering lower<mean<upper, eta_sq in (0,1)

columns.source: str, one of accommodation / indoor_attraction / outdoor_attraction / destination

output2.csv.description: one row, one-way ANOVA on the four robust-Z groups

columns.p_value: float, p-value (0.0 on underflow, see p_display in anova_detail.json)

supporting_artifacts.anova_detail.json: per-group median/MAD/robust_scale/z_mean/z_std/z_se/t_crit + F, p, eta_sq, omega_sq, df_between, df_within, ss_between, ss_within, ss_total

validation_checks: valid_n per source equals data_profile value exactly (else dtype issue, e.g. destination Rating read as text)
CI contains the mean and has positive width for all four sources
no NaN / inf in either output CSV; output1 has exactly 4 rows and output2 exactly 1 row
re-running the pipeline reproduces the values to 6 decimals (deterministic, no random component)
risks_and_caveats: Construct mismatch: FISETIO rating/rate are VENUE-level aggregates repeated monthly, while Airbnb and TripAdvisor are listing/transaction-level ratings. Row counts therefore overstate independent information for the attraction domains and inflate the F statistic; the venue-level sensitivity run is the mitigation.
Truncation: outdoors 'rate' has a hard 3.0 floor, so its 1-5 scale is censored and its small dispersion is an artefact, not evidence that park visits are more homogeneous in feeling.

Robust-Z destroys absolute level information by construction: after centring each domain on its own median, between-domain mean differences no longer express 'which domain users like more' in raw points. Report the raw 1-5 means side by side for the substantive ranking (raw means: accommodation 3.28 < destination 4.16 < indoor 4.38 < outdoor 4.67).
Very large n means p-values are near-zero for trivially small differences; lead with eta^2 (~0.019, small) and the pairwise Cohen's d, not with p.

Domain labels are heterogeneous across underlying populations (London museums/parks vs global Airbnb listings vs Indonesian tourist attractions) - any 'domain effect' is confounded with geography, price tier and measurement protocol.
Scipy dependency: if scipy is unavailable, compute F/p via the F survival function implemented with math.erfc/betainc or use a chi-square approximation and record the method.
key_findings_preview: ANOVA on robust-Z scores: F(3, 160798) = 1064.89, p < 1e-300, eta^2 = 0.0195 (small). Differences across the four domains are statistically decisive but explain only ~2% of variance; all 6 pairwise Welch comparisons are significant, with the largest gap between accommodation (z=+0.19) and indoor attractions (z=-0.65, Cohen's d=0.52). Raw-scale means order the domains accommodation 3.28 < destination 4.16 < indoor 4.38 < outdoor 4.67.
